heldBackBy.answer: My guess is the hidden CEP ceiling, plus STAND dropping every time I pushed for the top. I had maxed REP, INTEG and COMP, and it still was not enough, so it seems to be about being liked by the right people rather than doing well.

I think it was visibility. The game kept rewarding being seen (networking, townhalls) and I spent too many years doing quiet competent work. The 'safe pair of hands' rumour suggests I was seen as reliable rather than exciting, so I never got the next step up.
Nothing really held me back. I hit the top at 71 with maxed integrity, so if anything the game let me win. The Y7 refusal to tell me my ceiling was the only early friction and it didn't last.

Honestly, the game says it was never about me. Being a candidate in a ward seems to depend on the party, the ward and luck, not my stats. My COMP was 96 and I still lost. I suspect the ceiling was built in.

I think the game wanted me to be shown as too honest and too nice, since integrity hit 100 and I still lost the ward on 48.2%. My REP was 56 against the 60 I noted for a single seat, so I think I held myself back by picking the GRC route instead of building REP first. The CEP ceiling was probably in play too, but I never saw it rise.

I think it was my standing. I kept being honest and competent, but standing slid and I never got to be top of the pile. Asking about my ceiling or pay seemed to cost me too. I never really found out what the game wanted from me.

My guess is STAND, the stat that stayed in the 50s while everything else hit 100. Honesty maxed my reputation and integrity but didn't make the right people want me in the top jobs. The Leadership Programme snubs and the secret CEP ceiling probably capped me too, and the game never really told me which.

I think it was the hidden ceiling grade (CEP) and what the top thought of me, not how well I did. I was told I was steady and a safe pair of hands, which sounds like being kept useful rather than made PM.

Probably that secret ceiling grade (CEP) I learned about in Y18, plus being passed over for the Leadership Programme and Harvard early. My standing kept sliding even when I did the honest thing, so I suspect the game quietly caps you however well you play.

I think the game wants a political sponsor or a portfolio, and I kept choosing honesty and being seen over playing the game. My STAND slid for reasons it never told me, so I suspect being a straight talker made me useful but not trusted with a ministry.

Probably the hidden ceiling I noted in Y11 (CEP), plus my low STAND after I questioned the pay system in Cabinet. I also never got the dramatic politics route I wanted. Being honest all the time made me safe but dull.

The game says it was never about me, so probably the structure: the REP of 50 locked me out of the single-seat option and forced me into a team ward I lost. I also suspect I should have built visibility much earlier, which my reporting officer kept telling me and I kept ignoring.
I think my secret CEP capped me at Minister from the start, and my honesty kept draining STAND. I was a safe pair of hands, not someone they'd push to the very top.

My standing stayed at 40 because I gave honest answers in PQ and the game seems to penalise that. I never reached Prime Minister, and I suspect the game wants more visibility and networking than I gave it.
Low STAND from speaking up early and answering honestly. I still reached DPM, so it didn't block much. I think I just never got a PM-level invite and the game doesn't say what that needed.

My honesty cost me standing with seniors: the pay-indicator question, the honest PQ answer, and asking about my ceiling directly. I never got the secret CEP, which looked fixed from the start, so maybe nothing I did mattered much. I was rated 'steady' rather than a high flyer even with 100 integrity.

Low STAND the whole way, probably from the Leak confession and publishing raw feedback. It sat around 40 while everything else was maxed, so I think reputation with the system mattered more than integrity or competence.

I think it was STAND, which sank after the Y41 Facebook concession and never recovered, even though REP, INTEG and COMP were all at 100. Being honest at every turn probably cost me popularity with the people who pick the top job.

My STAND stat stayed low (around 41) while everything else was near maxed, so I suspect standing or political backing mattered more than competence. Also the game never let me see what CEP was, so I could never tell what the ceiling was.

Honestly, I don't think anything did. REP, INTEG and COMP were all at 100, and the only thing lagging was STAND, which I never understood. Maybe my blunt questions, like asking Cabinet about ministers' pay in Y38, cost me, but I still got to Minister.

Probably STAND, from asking awkward questions and being blunt even though my integrity was maxed. I think the game rewards being liked by the system over being right, and I never learned what COMP or STAND actually measure.

My honesty. Every time I disclosed, recused or asked an awkward question, INTEG and REP went up but STAND fell, and I suspect STAND is what gets you a portfolio. The hidden CEP ceiling probably played a part too.

The ceiling is built into the game: Permanent Secretary is the top of the civil service, and the next step is politics, which the game only ever hinted at. Appraisal wording also seemed to follow my reporting officer more than my stats, so maxed COMP, REP and INTEG didn't open the door.

Probably my bluntness with the bosses. Asking awkward questions kept costing STAND, and I put myself forward for succession at 71 when the game likely wanted me to back the other candidate. I also suspect the hidden CEP ceiling capped me no matter what.

Probably the Y43 succession bid, where I put myself forward and my STAND dipped, plus my blunt answers that kept costing STAND. I never got to be top dog, but I don't know if that was the cap or just how the game ended things.

I think it was the hidden CEP, my Currently Estimated Potential, plus STAND stuck low at 42 because I kept choosing family over late nights. Asking about my ceiling in Y5 probably hurt me too. The game never really explained which of these mattered most, so I'm guessing.
I think it was the STAND stat, which kept dipping because I chose concerts and family over work. Maybe the CEP capped me too, but the game never told me, so I can't say.

Probably STAND, whatever it is. Every honest answer to a PQ or Cabinet question lowered it, so my honesty seemingly cost me the top job. Maybe the CEP ceiling too, since the game never told me what mine was.

Probably STAND, which kept sliding whenever I gave straight answers or got promoted. I kept being honest and visible, and the game seemed to punish that in the one stat that mattered for going higher. I never worked out how to fix it.

I think it was STAND. My integrity, competence and reputation were all at 100, but public standing kept sliding because I always picked the honest option, so I stalled at Deputy PM. The game never told me what STAND needed.

Probably the election itself. My stats were maxed on integrity and competence, but reputation and standing were lower, so I think the game made politics a gamble that stats couldn't guarantee. Running in the GRC with a team may have been the weak spot, because I couldn't see how the team was doing.

STAND stayed at 50 the whole time, probably because of all the candour, and I think that is what stopped the politics invitation. Or the game simply never offers politics unless you pick one hidden thing, and I never found out what it was.

Nothing really held me back, since I reached Prime Minister by 61 with INTEG at 100. The only drag was STAND slowly bleeding from being straight, and it never actually cost me the top job. I was waiting for honesty to cost me something and it never did.

Honestly I don't know. I never became PM, and I couldn't tell whether that was my stand score dipping after I questioned Cabinet pay, or just that the game never offered the top job. I was never told what I was missing.

Mostly my own bluntness. Answering PQs straight and reading out rude questions kept costing STAND, so I was never the safe pick, and I was slower up the ladder than my scores suggested. Still got to the top though.

I lost the single seat by under two points, and the card said it was never about me, so apparently it was the party or the ward. I gambled on the solo seat instead of the GRC team, so that choice probably cost me. I never saw the satire remark or the missed concert come back, so it wasn't my integrity or those choices.
My REP stat was the weak one, and the game seemed to say the team and the ward mattered more than me. Maybe I should have built reputation earlier instead of stacking integrity and competence.

Mostly my own choices. Being honest and fixing things nobody asked for cost me STAND, but I still reached the top. The game never showed me what really held me back, and the glowing appraisals felt like they hid it.

Honestly, not much. Being straight with people cost me popularity (STAND) and I was passed over twice early on, but appraisals were always glowing and I still reached PM. If anything the game seemed to reward me for it.

Honestly, nothing held me back. I went from junior officer to PM by 59 with INTEGRITY 100. The only real setback was losing the GRC race by one REP point in Y9, and that barely slowed me. It felt like REP gated everything and I just kept it high.
Honestly nothing held me back, I got to PM at 60. If anything slowed me it was STAND, which dropped every time I was honest, so I had to dodge or network to catch up.

I don't think anything held me back, because I became Prime Minister at 59. The only drag was STAND, which kept sliding despite glowing appraisals, and I never learned why. My guess is that answering straight every year cost me something the game never explained.

My guess is that the Y38 succession bid got me quietly dropped from the Leadership Programme, and the leaks and the tea early on may have left a mark. But the game never said so, so it could just be a hidden rule that I was too honest or too outspoken for the top job.
Nothing really held me back, I got to PM at 61. If anything, the falling STAND was the drag, probably from that pay question and being too honest. But I never understood what STAND actually was.

Nothing really held me back. I reached the top at 59 with INTEG 100 and the game seemed to reward honesty every time. The only drag was STAND wobbling when I told the truth, which never cost me anything that mattered.
Honestly nothing did. I got to Prime Minister with 100 integrity, so the game mostly rewarded honesty and ambition. My STAND dropping a bit seemed to be the only brake, and it never mattered.

I think it was never being on the Leadership Programme list, plus the juniors getting the Harvard places instead of me. Honestly I'm not sure, because I got to Deputy PM anyway and the game never said what stopped me going higher.

Low STAND from being honest with seniors in PQs, not competence. I had 100 in REP, INTEG and COMP and still stopped at Deputy PM, so I think the game punishes candour with the people who choose the top job. I never got a clear explanation of how STAND actually works.
